title: Soundscapes Bird Song Study
outcome_scope: Short-term self-reported anxiety, depression and paranoia in healthy participants; not migraine or pain.
design: Randomized online experiment; 295 participants; four 6-minute conditions.
result_summary: Both birdsong groups reported less anxiety and paranoia after exposure; high-diversity birdsong also reduced depression. Traffic increased depression. Cognitive measures did not improve.
limitations: No neutral-sound control; acute exposure only. Diversity manipulation did not yield a clear differential benefit. A 30-second excerpt was not independently tested.
license_status: Unspecified for OSF audio. Open access article license does not establish a license for the repository audio or underlying bird recordings.
